newsitem.title: USA: State Department Cyprus envoy moves to new job.
newsitem.headline: State Department Cyprus envoy moves to new job.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said on Wednesday that special Cyprus coordinator James Williams was moving to another job, but said Washington planned to keep up efforts to resolve the Cyprus problem.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Williams would assume other duties as part of what he called a "normal rotation." He said he assumed Williams would be replaced by another official but could not say who that would be.

"This change in no way signifies any lessening of the administration's resolve to be helpful to the parties on Cyprus, to Greece, and Turkey and the Cypriot government itself," Burns told a news briefing.
Richard Beattie, President Bill Clinton's special emissary on Cyprus, will continue in his role, Burns added.

The State Department said last month it was considering a new diplomatic push to try to resolve the Cyprus problem as well as the Greco-Turkish dispute over the Aegean, but said no date had been set for any mission.

Cyprus has been divided between its Greek and Turkish communities since the northern third of the Mediterranean island was invaded in 1974 by Turkish mainland troops in response to a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia.
